explanation: The pole fires when the text names the person or organization that holds, governs or is responsible for the referent - its approver, supervisor, guardian, owner or kin - characteristically the phrase that introduces that party: 'of' after a grant/support noun (the approval of their supervisor, the consent of their male guardian, the support of the World Health Organization), 'from' in 'guidance from the teacher' or 'backing from the March of Dimes', 'by' in an ownership/control passive (owned by London Clubs, managed by the family), 'and his/her' before a relation noun (Stalin and his ministers), and the organization's controlling roles themselves (a change in management, the club's owners, chairman). It stays near zero when the same prepositions introduce an inanimate patient (the description of the building, the destruction of the city, the colour of the sky), a momentary or perceptual agent (mentioned by, seen by, admired by) or a merely possessed object (her car, her house), so the driver is the holder/authority role itself, not the preposition or the token alone.
